title: Severe muscle depletion in patients on the liver transplant wait list: Its prevalence and independent prognostic value
abstract: As detected by cross-sectional imaging, severe muscle depletion, which is termed sarcopenia, holds promise for prognostication in patients with cirrhosis. Our aims were to describe the prevalence and predictors of sarcopenia in patients with cirrhosis listed for liver transplantation (LT) and to determine its independent prognostic significance for the prediction of waiting-list mortality. Adults listed for LT who underwent abdominal computed tomography/magnetic resonance imaging within 6 weeks of activation were retrospectively identified. The exclusions were hepatocellular carcinoma, acute liver failure, prior LT, and listing for multivisceral transplantation or living related LT. Sixty percent of the 142 eligible patients were male, the median age was 53 years, and the median Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) score at listing was 15. Forty-one percent were sarcopenic; sarcopenia was more prevalent in males versus females (54% versus 21%, P < 0.001) and increased with the Child-Pugh class (10% for class A, 34% for class B, and 54% for class C, P = 0.007). Male sex, the dry-weight body mass index (BMI), and Child-Pugh class C cirrhosis (but not the MELD score) were independent predictors of sarcopenia. Sarcopenia was an independent predictor of mortality (hazard ratio = 2.36, 95% confidence interval = 1.23-4.53) after adjustments for age and MELD scores. In conclusion, sarcopenia is associated with increased waiting-list mortality and is poorly predicted by subjective nutritional assessment tools such as BMI and subjective global assessment. If this is validated in larger studies, the objective assessment of sarcopenia holds promise for prognostication in this patient population.

claims.text: Forty-one percent of eligible adult patients with cirrhosis listed for liver transplantation were sarcopenic.
Sarcopenia is significantly more prevalent in males than females among patients with cirrhosis listed for liver transplantation.
Sarcopenia prevalence increases with higher Child-Pugh class in patients with cirrhosis listed for liver transplantation.
Male sex, dry-weight body mass index, and Child-Pugh class C cirrhosis are independent predictors of sarcopenia in patients listed for liver transplantation.
Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) score is not an independent predictor of sarcopenia in patients listed for liver transplantation.
Sarcopenia is an independent predictor of waiting-list mortality after adjustments for age and MELD scores in patients listed for liver transplantation.
Sarcopenia is poorly predicted by subjective nutritional assessment tools such as body mass index and subjective global assessment.

limitations.text: The findings require validation in larger studies.

future_work.text: Validation of objective sarcopenia assessment in larger studies for prognostication in liver transplant candidates.

methodologies.name: Retrospective cohort study using cross-sectional imaging
methodologies.description: Retrospective identification and analysis of adults listed for liver transplantation who underwent abdominal CT or MRI within 6 weeks of activation to evaluate sarcopenia prevalence, predictors, and waiting-list mortality.
conditions: Adults listed for liver transplantation with abdominal CT/MRI within 6 weeks of activation
Excluded listing for multivisceral transplantation or living related liver transplantation
